questions.question: How do scientists calculate global surface temperatures?
options: By taking tens of thousands of measurements worldwide
By relying solely on satellite images of the polar ice caps
By measuring the temperature at a single central station in Europe
By estimating temperatures based on historical weather diaries

questions.question: What has been the trend in overall global surface temperatures since the industrial revolution in the 1850s?
options: They have been steadily decreasing.
They have remained completely stable.
They have been increasing.
They have fluctuated with no overall trend.

questions.question: Which of the following provide scientists with data on longer-term temperature changes before modern records began?
options: Tree rings and ice cores
Volcanic ash layers and desert sand depth
Fossilized animal footprints and sea shells
Ancient stone structures and cave paintings

questions.question: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas that is released by living organisms and also produced when burning fuels?
options: Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen gas
Argon gas
Helium gas

questions.question: How does methane compare to carbon dioxide as a greenhouse gas?
options: Methane is a more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide.
Methane is less potent than carbon dioxide.
Both gases have exactly the same warming effect per molecule.
Methane does not contribute to the greenhouse effect at all.

questions.question: What is the primary effect of greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere?
options: They block all solar radiation from entering the atmosphere.
They keep the atmosphere warmer than it would be without them.
They cause the atmosphere to gradually lose its oxygen.
They reflect all heat back into outer space.

questions.question: How does the melting of land-based ice sheets due to increased temperatures affect the oceans?
options: It moves more water into the sea, causing sea levels to rise.
It decreases the total volume of water in the sea.
It has no effect on sea levels because the ice is already in the water.
It causes sea levels to fall by cooling the water.

questions.question: Why does the melting of sea ice in summer not raise sea levels?
options: Sea ice is made of fresh water which takes up less space than salt water.
Melting sea ice does not add water to the sea because it is already floating in it.
The water from melted sea ice immediately evaporates into the air.
Sea ice melts into underground reservoirs instead of the ocean.

questions.question: Apart from melting ice sheets, what is another major cause of sea level rise as global temperatures increase?
options: Warmer oceans and seas expand, causing sea levels to rise.
Increased rainfall over the ocean surface.
An increase in the speed of ocean currents.
Underwater volcanic eruptions displacing water.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares fuel use in petrol/diesel vehicles and electric vehicles?
options: Petrol and diesel vehicles burn fuels, while electric vehicles do not, though fuels may be burned to generate electricity.
Electric vehicles burn fuel internally to run their heaters, while petrol vehicles do not.
Both electric and petrol vehicles must burn fuel onboard to move.
Neither electric nor petrol vehicles require any fuel burning at any stage.

questions.question: What is a major limitation of carbon capture and storage (CCS) technology?
options: It can reduce carbon dioxide emissions but is very expensive.
It actually increases the amount of carbon dioxide released into the atmosphere.
It can only be used on electric vehicles.
It has been proven to be chemically impossible to separate carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of global greenhouse gas emissions is produced by the energy sector?
options: About 10%
About 25%
About 50%
About 75%

questions.question: How do a car's weight and speed affect the energy it uses to travel 100 km?
options: Cars use more energy if they are heavier or travel at higher speeds.
Cars use less energy if they are heavier or travel at higher speeds.
Weight and speed have no effect on the energy used by a car.
Heavier cars use less energy, but higher speeds increase energy use.

questions.question: How does tyre pressure affect a car's energy consumption?
options: Cars use less energy if their tyres are inflated to the correct air pressure.
Cars use more energy when their tyres are correctly inflated.
Tyre pressure only affects safety, not energy use.
Fully deflated tyres use the least amount of energy.

questions.question: How do solar panels differ from many other electricity generation methods?
options: They produce electricity without electric generators.
They require a steam turbine to spin a coil of wire.
They generate electricity by burning biomass.
They must use falling water to produce a current.

questions.question: What can be used to spin turbines in order to generate electricity?
options: Falling water or wind
Magnetic fields alone without any movement
Solar radiation directly hitting the turbine blades
Chemical batteries connected to the generator shaft
